question: Can the single end-free port graph learn a new preference that is orthogonal rather than a sign flip, and does that experience affect action through the learned graph itself?
policy: Use the sealed 16-node tanh joint recipe previously selected on stable/reversal development for the native port graph. All graph weights and growth/retirement remain available throughout real teaching. No per-life examples table, feature expansion, task ID, change indicator, or external action learning head.
design: Draw private unit vector A in four chemical dimensions and an independent random direction B orthogonal to A. Two sign twins start with the same A, same food mixtures, body geometry, exploration noise, taste draws and brain. Each subsequent B food has exactly opposite realized taste across the two worlds, with its expected preference given by +B or -B. Return restores A. No physical taste on the last 64 NEW foods per stage. Timeout counts as failure.
primary: B silent-tail optimal contact minus 0.5; B silent-tail joint minus yoke with independent fair signs; B silent-tail intact minus endpoint fork with other twin's entire learned synaptic matrix and support. Simultaneous 95% Bonferroni percentile intervals, paired crossed bootstrap on eight birth roots and sixteen world roots. For interchange, fork at the same pre-probe boundary and preserve the recipient's activity. Additionally report just-state exchange (recipient synapses intact), both twins making correct opposite choices, first B action invariant, A and A-return, and edits. Silent worlds are not fed back into the live path.
limits: Orthogonal linear utilities on never-repeated continuous chemical mixtures test an unfamiliar direction rather than an arbitrary nonlinear function. A/B habitats have no context label. Swapping matrix and support together identifies the effect of the learned synaptic graph, not any specific edge or bidirectionality requirement.
